title: Building n-Dimensional Trees for Resolution-Based Progressive Compression
problem: Strict error bounds in floating-point compression yield large files; users may not need full fidelity data
motivation: Progressive data access enables users to download initial fidelity then request higher fidelities on-demand
method: Progressive compression organizes floating-point data into n-dimensional trees—hierarchical structures spanning multiple data dimensions—where traversing deeper into the tree adds accuracy to the data. Users can stop at any depth to get a version with just enough precision for their needs, rather than being forced to download full-precision data that may be wastefully large. This approach trades off file size against data quality based on what accuracy each user actually requires.
key_novelty: Using hierarchical trees lets users choose their needed accuracy level when loading compressed data, rather than requiring full-precision compression in all cases.
contributions: Develops n-dimensional tree structures for progressive compression
Demonstrates competitive compression ratios vs. traditional methods
Analyzes quality impact of resolution progression
limitations: Limited evaluation details; unclear performance on various data types
